Flox draws from the Flox Catalog (built on nixpkgs), which carries **millions of historical package-version combinations**. So rather than memorizing a list, you discover what's available with two commands:

```bash
flox search postgresql       # find the PostgreSQL package(s)
flox show postgresql          # list every available version of a package
```

## Solution: Layer the environments at runtime (don't compose them)

What you want is **layered activation**, not composition. Composition (`[include]`) merges manifests into one at build time — exactly what you're trying to avoid. Layering keeps each environment's `.flox/` and manifest completely separate; you just activate one *on top of* the other. Each keeps its own packages, vars, hooks, and services, and Flox stacks them on your `PATH` (later activations take precedence).

So the key is: **do nothing special in the manifests.** No `[include]` block. You just create two independent environments and nest the `flox activate` calls.

### The `debug-tools` manifest

Create this as a standalone environment (e.g. in `~/envs/debug-tools`). Note there's no `[include]` — that's the whole point:

```toml

[install]
gdb.pkg-path = "gdb"
strace.pkg-path = "strace"
lsof.pkg-path = "lsof"
htop.pkg-path = "htop"
jq.pkg-path = "jq"
ripgrep.pkg-path = "ripgrep"

# Namespace vars so they never collide with the base env

[options]
systems = ["x86_64-linux", "aarch64-linux", "x86_64-darwin", "aarch64-darwin"]
```
